answer: New identities start at a low vertex of the trust graph and can only climb by completing peer-verified tasks. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity binding: each agent must lock a bond that scales with claimed reputation. A violet badge marks fully bonded participants; a yarrow token flags probationary ones. Creating N fake identities costs N bonds plus forfeiture risk on every fraudulent attestation, so attackers pay linearly while honest peers earn yield, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0033's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
